tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Return the open meeting slots a Lucie Sync host offers, plus their booking rules (durations offered, minimum notice, how far ahead you can book, buffer between meetings). Returns only bookable slots and policy — never the host's raw calendar. Use this to find a time before proposing one to the user. Slots are absolute instants (ISO-8601 UTC). Pass the booker's viewerTimeZone so times display in THEIR local zone — the booker should never have to do time-zone math.

handle.description: The host's booking handle, e.g. "@alice" or "alice" (from their lucie.network/book/@<handle> link). The leading @ is optional.

durationMinutes.description: Desired meeting length in minutes. Must be one the host offers. Defaults to 30 if omitted.

viewerTimeZone.description: The booker's IANA time zone, e.g. "Asia/Singapore" or "America/New_York". Pass the booker's own zone so slots are shown in their local time. Defaults to the host's zone if omitted.

from.description: ISO-8601 start of the search window. Defaults to now + the host's minimum notice.

to.description: ISO-8601 end of the search window. Defaults to the host's max-advance horizon.

fromHour.description: Only times starting at or after this hour (0–23) in viewerTimeZone. Use with toHour whenever the user asks for part of the day, e.g. mornings 9–12, afternoons 12–17, after work 17–21, so the times you list and the calendar link match.

toHour.description: Only times ending by this hour (1–24) in viewerTimeZone. See fromHour.

tools.name: book_meeting
tools.description: Book a confirmed meeting on a Lucie Sync host's calendar at a specific start time. This is a real write: it creates a calendar event and emails both the host and the booker. Always call check_availability first and use one of the open slots it returns. Before calling, (1) show the booker the specific date/time you're about to book — in their own time zone — and get their explicit confirmation, and (2) collect their name, email, AND a brief reason for the meeting (ask for the reason if not given; it's required and shared with the host).

handle.description: The host's booking handle, e.g. "@alice" or "alice" (the leading @ is optional).

startLocal.description: The start as the user reads it, in viewerTimeZone, copied verbatim from the slot list (e.g. "Thu, Nov 20, 2:00 PM PST"). This is what the approval screen shows the user; it must be the same moment as startAt or nothing is booked.

startAt.description: The exact ISO-8601 `start` value copied verbatim from a check_availability slot (an absolute UTC instant, e.g. 2026-07-28T17:00:00Z). Do NOT construct this from a local wall-clock time the booker said — that risks the wrong time zone; always copy the slot's start.

durationMinutes.description: Meeting length in minutes. Must be one the host offers.

bookerName.description: Full name of the person the meeting is for (the booker).

bookerEmail.description: The booker's email. The confirmation and calendar invite are sent here.

reason.description: A short description of why the booker wants to meet (the agenda / purpose). Required — ask the booker for it before booking. Shared with the host alongside the invite.

viewerTimeZone.description: The BOOKER's IANA time zone (e.g. America/New_York) — the same one you passed to check_availability. Their confirmation email and reminders are written in this zone, so without it they read the host's zone instead and have to do the time-zone maths themselves.

tools.name: find_group_times
tools.description: Given several Lucie hosts (by @handle), return the meeting times when ALL of them are free — the intersection of their availability — for a meeting of the given length. Read-only: never books, never exposes anyone's raw calendar (only the shared open slots). Use it before book_group_meeting, to pick a time to BOOK: it only works in lengths every host's booking page offers, and every participant needs a Lucie handle. To create a poll (a Sync) for people to vote on, do NOT use this as a pre-check: call create_group_event (times) or create_trip_sync (days) directly; they handle any length and people without a Lucie handle. Times are absolute instants; pass viewerTimeZone so they show in the organizer's local zone.

handles.description: The participants' booking handles, e.g. ["@alice", "@bob"]. The leading @ is optional.

durationMinutes.description: Meeting length in minutes. Must be one every participant offers. Defaults to 30.

viewerTimeZone.description: The organizer's IANA time zone, e.g. "America/New_York". Common times are shown in this zone. Defaults to UTC.

from.description: ISO-8601 start of the search window.

to.description: ISO-8601 end of the search window.

fromHour.description: Only times starting at or after this hour (0–23) in viewerTimeZone. Use with toHour whenever the user asks for part of the day, e.g. mornings 9–12, afternoons 12–17, after work 17–21, so the times you list and the calendar link match.

toHour.description: Only times ending by this hour (1–24) in viewerTimeZone. See fromHour.

tools.name: create_group_event
tools.description: Create a Sync (what Lucie Sync calls a scheduling poll; the app's "Find a time" button, formerly "group event") for a CALL or an IN-PERSON MEETING, where people vote on TIMES. Use it for "create a sync", "find a time with @sam", "set up coffee with…". For a trip, offsite, conference, retreat or any full-day or multi-day event, where people vote on DAYS, use create_trip_sync instead, not this tool. kind "call" (default) adds a Google Meet link when sent; kind "in_person_meeting" takes `place` and the organizer's `travelMinutes` each way, and only proposes times that leave room for the trip. durationMinutes can be any length up to 480; candidate times come from when every listed @handle is free for that whole length. Call it directly; don't pre-check with check_availability or find_group_times (those are for booking, in fixed lengths). The organizer's own calendar always counts; other participants' count if they have a Lucie @handle, and anyone else just votes on the link, so a missing handle never blocks a poll. Returns a vote link. Creates the poll only: no emails, no calendar writes. Confirm title, participants, kind, place and length with the organizer first. Sync Pro (or a Lucie Membership).

title.description: The meeting title, e.g. "Q3 planning sync".

kind.description: Read first. "call" (default): people vote on times, Meet link added. "in_person_meeting": people vote on times at a place. For a trip or multi-day event use the create_trip_sync tool instead.

handles.description: Other participants' Lucie @handles, if they have one, so their calendars count when picking times. The organizer's own handle is added automatically. People without a Lucie handle do NOT go here and don't block anything: they just vote on the link.

organizerName.description: The organizer's name (shown on the poll).

durationMinutes.description: call / in_person_meeting only: meeting length in minutes, ANY length up to 480 (e.g. 120 for a dinner); it doesn't have to be a length the participants' booking pages offer. Defaults to 30. Never use this for a trip: use tripDays.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone for the poll's displayed times, e.g. "America/New_York". Defaults to UTC.

from.description: ISO-8601 start of the search window.

to.description: ISO-8601 end of the search window.

place.description: Where, for in_person_meeting or trip, e.g. "Blue Bottle, Mint Plaza, San Francisco" or "Lisbon". Shown to voters.

travelMinutes.description: in_person_meeting only: the organizer's travel time EACH WAY, one of 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120. Only times leaving room for the trip are proposed, and the trip is blocked on their calendar once sent.

tripDays.description: trip only: how many days it lasts. Defaults to 1.

dates.description: trip only, REQUIRED: the candidate start days to offer, as YYYY-MM-DD, up to 10, e.g. ["2027-01-05","2027-01-12"]. Can be any distance ahead.

tools.name: create_trip_sync
tools.description: Create a Sync where people vote on DAYS, not times: a trip, offsite, retreat, conference, workshop, or any full-day or multi-day event ("which week works for the Lisbon offsite?", "3-day offsite sometime Jan–Mar", "which day for the workshop?"). Give tripDays (how many days it lasts; 1 for a single full day) and dates: the candidate START days as YYYY-MM-DD, up to 10, any distance ahead. If the user gives a range ("sometime in January"), pick a few sensible start days in it (e.g. one per week, avoiding the user's stated constraints) and confirm them with the user first. Optional place (a city or venue). Returns a vote link; anyone can vote, with or without a Lucie handle. Creates the poll only: no emails, no calendar writes. Sync Pro (or a Lucie Membership) via the personal connector.

title.description: The trip or event name, e.g. "Q1 offsite".

tripDays.description: How many days it lasts. 1 for a single full day.

dates.description: Candidate START days, YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. ["2027-01-05","2027-01-12","2027-01-19"]. Any distance ahead.

organizerName.description: The organizer's name (shown on the poll).

handles.description: Participants' @handles, if they have them (for the summary only; their availability isn't checked for trips).

place.description: A city or venue, e.g. "Lisbon". Shown to voters.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles". Defaults to UTC.

tools.name: book_group_meeting
tools.description: Confirm a group meeting at a specific time across several Lucie hosts (by @handle), creating ONE shared Google Calendar event with everyone invited. YOU (the connector's owner) are the organizer and host the event on your calendar — no organizer handle needed. This is a real write: it re-verifies every participant (you included) is free at that instant and refuses if anyone isn't — so it never double-books. Always call find_group_times first and copy an exact common-slot start. Before calling, confirm the time (in each person's zone), the participants, the title, and the reason. Requires you to be on Sync Pro (or a Lucie Membership) via your personal connector; everyone must have a live booking page.

participantHandles.description: The other participants' @handles, e.g. ["@lucie", "@taylor"]. Each must have a live Lucie booking page. Leading @ optional.

startLocal.description: The start as the user reads it, in viewerTimeZone, copied verbatim from the slot list (e.g. "Thu, Nov 20, 2:00 PM PST"). This is what the approval screen shows the user; it must be the same moment as startAt or nothing is booked.

startAt.description: The exact ISO-8601 `start` copied verbatim from a find_group_times common slot (absolute UTC instant). Do NOT construct it from a wall-clock time.

durationMinutes.description: Meeting length in minutes. Must be one the organizer offers.

title.description: The meeting title, e.g. "Q3 planning sync".

reason.description: A short agenda/purpose, shared with everyone on the invite.

viewerTimeZone.description: The organizer's IANA time zone (e.g. America/Los_Angeles), the one startLocal is written in.
